sections.label: Taxi and PHC journeys share
sections.summary: About 6% of all journeys are completed on taxis or PHCs, which form the point-to-point sector.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Today, about 6% of all journeys are completed on taxis or PHCs, which make up the point-to-point (P2P) sector.

sections.label: Taxi and PHC numbers, ride-hail share
sections.summary: There are about 20,000 taxis and 45,000 PHCs, and over two-thirds of P2P trips are ride-hail, 30% by taxis.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Today, there are about 20,000 taxis and 45,000 PHCs, providing many more P2P options and improved service standards.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Today, more than two-thirds of all P2P are ride-hail trips, of which 30% are carried out by taxis.

sections.label: Taxi booking waiting time fall
sections.summary: Taxi booking waiting time fell by about two minutes in 2016, to just under seven minutes in 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: For example, the waiting time for a taxi booking has fallen by about two minutes in 2016, to just under seven minutes in 2018.

sections.label: Licensing PHC booking service operators
sections.summary: PHC booking service operators will be licensed.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: First, we will license PHC booking service operators.

sections.label: Separate street-hail and ride-hail regulations
sections.summary: One set of regulations will cover all street-hail services and a different set all ride-hail services, regardless of vehicle type.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Given the growing proportion of ride-hail trips, it makes better sense to have one set of regulations for all street-hail services and a different set of regulations for all ride-hail services, regardless of the type of vehicle used.

sections.label: Licensing ride-hail operators by fleet size
sections.summary: Street-hail operators keep the requirement, ride-hail operators with 800 or more vehicles will be licensed, and those with fewer than 800 exempted.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Moving forward, this requirement will continue to be imposed for street-hail service operators – no change.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: We will also license all ride-hail service operators with 800 or more vehicles on their platform.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Ride-hail service operators with fewer than 800 vehicles on their platform will be exempted from the need to obtain a licence.

sections.label: Penalties for conviction
sections.summary: A convicted person may face a fine of up to $10,000, imprisonment of up to six months, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: If convicted, they may face a fine of up to $10,000, imprisonment of up to six months, or both.

sections.label: Light regulatory approach for operators
sections.summary: LTA will adopt a light regulatory approach and intends to prohibit operators from offering exclusive arrangements that lock in drivers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: As the market has evolved, LTA will adopt a light regulatory approach towards service standards and will streamline regulatory requirements where possible.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: We intend to prohibit operators from offering exclusive arrangements to "lock in" drivers that, in effect, prevent them from driving for other operators.

sections.label: Standard regulatory provisions and penalties
sections.summary: The Bill includes record-keeping and data requirements, with non-compliant operators liable for financial penalties, suspension or licence revocation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: The Bill also includes other standard regulatory provisions, such as requirements for operators to keep records, and to provide relevant information and data to LTA.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Operators who fail to comply with LTA’s regulatory requirements will be liable for financial penalties, suspension or even revocation of their licences.

sections.label: Extending fare regulation to PHC
sections.summary: The PTC Act is amended to give PTC powers to extend the taxi fare regulatory approach to PHC fares.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Given the rising proportion of trips by PHCs, we are amending the Public Transport Council Act (PTC Act) to give PTC the powers to extend today’s taxi fare regulatory approach to PHC fares.

sections.label: Fare evasion and overcharging offences
sections.summary: The PTC Act is amended so fare evasion and overcharging offences extend to PHC trips booked through licensed ride-hail operators.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: In addition, we will amend the PTC Act such that the offences of fare evasion and overcharging extend to PHC trips booked through licensed ride-hail service operators.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Lastly, the Bill makes related and consequential amendments to update provisions in certain Acts and to clarify our regulatory intent.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: We will open licence applications for street-hail and ride-hail service operators in February 2020, and the new regulatory framework will commence in June 2020.

sections.label: Private hire and taxi driver numbers
sections.summary: Singapore has over 40,000 private hire and 100,000 taxi drivers, serving over 1.2 million daily trips.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Fast forward to today, we have over 40,000 private hire and 100,000 taxi drivers in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Together they serve over 1.2 million daily trips, up from where we had only taxis which served a million trips a day.

sections.label: Regulating private hire operators
sections.summary: Only taxi operators face regulatory controls, and LTA will now regulate private hire operators as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Currently, as we have heard from Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary, only taxi operators are subjected to regulatory controls.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We have previously called for, and I am glad that LTA will now regulate the private hire operators as well.

sections.label: Tripartite Standards licensing compliance
sections.summary: It recommends that all operators comply with the Tripartite Standards as part of licensing requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding these initiatives, we recommend that all operators comply with the Tripartite Standards as part of the licensing requirements.

sections.label: Reviewing taxi standards and exclusivity
sections.summary: Taxi Availability framework and Quality of Service standards will be reviewed, and the new framework will seek to prohibit driver exclusivity arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We are not short of local drivers, Mr Speaker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: They have done quite a fair bit, but I am glad to hear today that they will be reviewing the Taxi Availability framework and the Quality of Service standards for taxi operators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: With the current fleet of private hire vehicles exceeding more than twice the number of taxis, I am glad that the new standards will be reviewed and rationalised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am also very happy to hear that the new regulatory framework will seek to prohibit driver exclusivity arrangements by all parties.

sections.label: Abuse on private hire carpool platforms
sections.summary: LTA needs to pay attention to possible abuse on private hire carpool platforms, where drivers need no vocational licence and could join several platforms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: LTA also needs to pay particular attention to possible abuse on the private hire carpool platforms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: These drivers need not possess a vocational licence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: But because of no regulatory control in this market space, a driver could possibly join several platforms and take on multiple trips beyond the stipulated daily limits.

sections.label: Bill recognises ride-hail providers
sections.summary: The Bill is a proper recognition that ride-hail providers play a big role in the transport ecosystem and deserve to be regulated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Bill before us today is not the first time the Ministry of Transport (MOT) and LTA have sought to regulate such services, but this Bill is finally a proper recognition of the fact that ride-hail providers do play a big role in our transport ecosystem and deserve to be regulated as such.

sections.label: CCCS directions and Grab market
sections.summary: It asks whether CCCS directions would continue and whether the Bill loosens restraints by redefining the market Grab operates in.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Should this Bill pass, would the CCCS directions continue to be in force?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Noting that the regulatory framework set forth is one of harmonising regulations between street-hail and ride-hail operators, will the Bill loosen the current restraints via redefining the market that Grab operates in as a P2P transport operator, rather than just a ride-hail platform?

sections.label: PTC ride-hail fare regulation
sections.summary: Clauses 58, 59 and 60 let PTC regulate ride-hail providers on fares, raising the question of algorithm transparency versus hard rules like surge caps.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: On a related note, clauses 58, 59 and 60 of the Bill will allow PTC to regulate ride-hail service providers, notably on the issue of fares as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Will it be one aimed to make transparent the algorithms that power the fare structures, or will it be one that will institute hard rules, such as surge pricing caps or standardising the fare per kilometre travelled?

sections.label: In-car recording privacy concerns
sections.summary: Passenger and driver behaviour has made headlines, and though LTA allows in-car video and audio recording, privacy concerns remain as PDPA retention guidelines are vague.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Negative behaviour by passengers and drivers alike have made for regular headlines in recent times, spurred by the proliferation of smart devices, both handheld and in-car.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, as LTA allows for in-car video recording in 2018 and audio recording just last month, privacy concerns still remain.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) guidelines are still vague on the retention of such data, only noting that the data be no longer retained when it is no longer necessary for business or legal purposes.

sections.label: Unused private hire cars
sections.summary: After Uber departed, industry experts put the number of unused cars in the private hire fleet at over 2,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: When Uber departed, the end result was not pretty as well, as industry experts place the number of unused cars in the private hire fleet at over 2,000.

sections.label: New COE category for P2P vehicles
sections.summary: Vehicles owned by or leased to P2P passenger transport operators should get a new COE category so they do not distort COE prices for private car owners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: With such big players having the uneven power to distort COE prices, vehicles owned by or leased to all P2P passenger transport operators should be subject to a new category of COE so that these vehicles will not affect or drive COE pricing for current categories, to the detriment of private car owners.

sections.label: Taxi and PHC fleet sizes
sections.summary: Singapore's taxi fleet fell from 28,000 to 19,000 as of last month, while the PHC fleet rose from almost zero to 50,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In Singapore, the total taxi fleet has decreased from the height of 28,000 to 19,000 as of last month, while the PHC fleet has increased from almost zero to 50,000, so maybe 50,000 times.

sections.label: PTC ride-hail fare pricing policy
sections.summary: Clause 59 amends Part 5 of the Public Transport Council Act to let PTC impose a ride-hail fare pricing policy fixing fare components, surge pricing factors and price limits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Interestingly, clause 59 of the current Bill, Part 5 of the Public Transport Council Act, is amended to allow PTC to impose a ride-hail fare pricing policy that, amongst other things, fixes the components of ride-hail fares, specifying the factor or factors to be applied, which is more commonly referred to as surge pricing, and fixes a maximum or minimum price or price range.

sections.label: PHC and taxi driver rules
sections.summary: PHC drivers can be 21 and take a one-day course, while taxi drivers must be 30, take a two-day course and be Singaporean.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: First, PHC drivers can be as young as 21 years old while the minimum age to qualify as a taxi driver is 30.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: PHC drivers only need to pass a one-day course, but taxi drivers need to pass a two-day course.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: On the other hand, a taxi driver must be a Singaporean and no PR is allowed.

sections.label: Clause 59 ride-hail fare non-payment
sections.summary: Clause 59 amends the PTC Act offence of non-payment of ride-hail or street-hail fare, which debit card users with insufficient funds get away with.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Clause 59 of the Bill seeks to amend the PTC Act, which spells out an offence of non-payment of ride-hail or street-hail fare under section 24D of the PTC Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, many debit card users attempt to pay the ride-hail fare even though there is insufficient fund in their bank accounts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: They get away with non-payment of the ride-hail fares as banks can only verify their bank balances after they have left the vehicles.

sections.label: Bill to regulate ride-hailing operators
sections.summary: With the growing number of PHCs, LTA is introducing this Bill to regulate ride-hailing service operators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: With the growing number of PHCs, LTA is finally introducing this Bill to regulate ride-hailing service operators.

sections.label: PHC drivers' traffic offence appeals
sections.summary: Residents typically appeal to waive one or two traffic offences, but PHC drivers commonly appeal for more than 10, reflecting PHCs' early traits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Residents typically see me to appeal to waive one or two traffic offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: However, it is not uncommon for PHC drivers to see me to appeal for more than 10 traffic offences, a reflection of PHCs' traits in their early days.

sections.label: PTC setting ride-hail fares
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether MOT intends to ask PTC to set maximum and minimum fares for ride-hail service operators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Meanwhile, I would like to know whether MOT has the intention of asking PTC to set the maximum and minimum fares for the ride-hail service operators.

sections.label: Harmonising taxi and PHC regulations
sections.summary: The speaker says harmonising taxi and PHC regulations is needed for a level playing field, safer services, and to review COE bidding exemptions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I have been waiting for the P2P Passenger Transport Industry Bill for a long time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I think it is necessary to harmonise the regulations of taxi and PHC operators in order to create a more level playing field and provide safer and more satisfactory passenger services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We should review and harmonise the market as existing taxi operators are exempted from COE bidding while ride-hail operators need to bid for COE.

sections.label: LTA licensing and PTC fare regulation
sections.summary: LTA will issue street-hail and ride-hail licences, with PTC regulating fees, fare calculation and charges, making dynamic peak-period billing more transparent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Henceforth, under LTA's new licensing framework, two types of licences will be issued, which will be according to street-hail service or ride-hail service, and the fees for both services will be regulated by PTC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: With PTC regulating the fares, the way fares are calculated and the range of charges, particularly the dynamic billing introduced during peak periods, will be more transparent and give passengers greater peace of mind.

sections.label: Driver benefits, licensing and Grab share
sections.summary: The passage asks about driver employment benefits and security, suggests licensing only Singaporeans, notes licensing and no-exclusivity provisions, and cites Grab's estimated 80% share.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: What employment benefits and security do these drivers enjoy, such as MediSave and MediShield Life?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I suggest that only Singaporeans are allowed to be licensed drivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Notable provisions include the requirement for all providers to be licensed and the prohibition of driver exclusivity arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I have a few clarifications to seek and suggestions to make.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I note that within the PHC sector, Grab currently has a market share that has been estimated at approximately 80% last year.

sections.label: PTC ride-hail pricing and fixed options
sections.summary: The Bill gives PTC power to regulate and set ride-hail pricing, and the passage asks whether fixed pricing options will remain alongside dynamic pricing for commuters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Next, the Bill gives the PTC the power to regulate and set pricing policies for ride-hail services for the first time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In this context, I would like to ask if the regulatory regime for all P2P services will continue to require there to be fixed pricing options available to commuters within the P2P ecosystem, in addition to dynamic pricing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Dynamic pricing efficiently matches demand and supply, going by classical economic considerations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, notwithstanding the means-tested persons with disabilities (PWDs) taxi subsidy scheme, a fixed pricing option on offer within the P2P industry ecosystem is still of value to lower-income persons who may have ambulatory problems, for example, PWDs.

sections.label: Taxi and private hire vehicle numbers
sections.summary: Taxi population fell from 28,736 in 2014 to 20,581 in 2018, while private hire chauffeured cars rose to 45,342.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2014, before the private hire platforms started offering transport services, the taxi population stood at 28,736 vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: By 2018, the taxi population fell to 20,581 vehicles but the number of private hire chauffeured cars rose to 45,342.

sections.label: Private hire share of P2P spending
sections.summary: In the Household Expenditure Survey 2017/2018, private hire services account for 38 cents of every dollar spent on P2P transport.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the recently released Household Expenditure Survey 2017/2018, private hire services now account for 38 cents out of every dollar spent on P2P transport services.

sections.label: Section 35 licence penalties
sections.summary: Section 35 lets LTA revoke a licence or levy a penalty of up to 10% of annual turnover or $100,000 for specified lapses, including inadequate service.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The teeth of these regulations are in section 35 which authorises LTA to revoke a licence, or levy a penalty that could be up to 10% of annual turnover or $100,000, for specified lapses.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Consider that section 35(1)(d) allows LTA to take action if the licensee fails to provide, and I quote, "adequate and satisfactory street-hail or ride-hail service".

sections.label: Ride-hailing efficiency research papers
sections.summary: Two papers find ride-hailing matching raises utilisation and cuts wait times compared with traditional taxis.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In a paper "Disruptive Change in the Taxi Business: The Case of Uber" published in the American Economic Review in 2016, Cramer and Krueger find that in the US, private-hire cars are 38% more utilised than traditional taxis.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This gain is because ride-hailing software makes matching faster and more efficient; traditional taxis in the US have to cruise for commuters or be dispatched by phone call.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This increase in productivity means that fares could be 28% less and driver hourly earnings would be the same.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In a paper "Frictions in a Competitive, Regulated Market: Evidence from Taxis" published in the American Economic Review in 2019, Frechette et al model the New York City taxi market, which is entirely street-hail.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They show that a perfect ride-hailing matching system would increase trips and reduce wait times by about 13%.

sections.label: Grab-Uber merger competition fine
sections.summary: CCCS fined Grab and Uber $13 million as their 2018 merger lessened competition and raised effective fares.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: CCCS fined Grab and Uber $13 million because their merger in 2018 led to a substantial lessening of competition.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Effective fares went up between 10% to 15% after the merger, largely through the withdrawal of discounts.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To harness the efficiency gains of technology and network economies, ride-hailing platforms need the largest possible reach.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But when they have such reach, they have great market power and they can abuse this in ways that can be hard to detect.

sections.label: Harmonising street-hail and ride-hail codes
sections.summary: The first principle suggested is harmonising Codes of Practice so street-hail and ride-hail licensees are treated evenly.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The first principle I suggest is harmonisation of the Codes of Practice and other aspects of regulation, to ensure that street-hail and ride-hail licensees are treated as evenly as possible, to ensure that competition across licensees for drivers and commuters is as active and innovative as possible.

sections.label: Price regulation as last resort
sections.summary: The Government is urged to use price and quantity regulation only as a last resort against market power abuses.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Some drivers are committed to driving for a given platform, but many more are casual drivers who switch platforms rapidly.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to engage the industry with a view to ensuring that price and quantity regulation is used only as a last resort, to protect the public against abuses of market power, and not as a means of creating unnecessary differentiation among licensees.

sections.label: Clarifying competition regulation responsibilities
sections.summary: The Ministry should clarify how competition issues are regulated, since both CCCS and MOT have responsibility.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The taxi industry was characterised by a dominant player for many years.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is important for the Ministry to clarify how competition issues will be regulated, given that both CCCS and MOT have responsibility over the sector.

sections.label: Bill regulating P2P passenger transport
sections.summary: The speaker's views are personal, and the Bill is intended to regulate P2P passenger transport services in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: However, my views expressed today are my own, based on interaction with some residents and the feedback I received.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: This Bill is intended to regulate the provision of P2P passenger transport services in Singapore.

sections.label: Driver anxiety over new Bill
sections.summary: Drivers feel anxiety about the new Bill and regulations, with concerns about sections 30 and 31.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: There is some anxiety from among the drivers about what this new Bill and further regulations would bring.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I believe in this respect, there may be concerns with regard to what sections 30 and 31 of this draft Bill would mean to the drivers.

sections.label: PHC drivers enter ERP fares
sections.summary: PHC drivers currently enter additional fares such as ERP manually into the passenger's eventual charge.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In this regard, there are some specific anecdotes that I would like to share.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I am told that currently, PHC drivers enter additional fares, such as ERP, manually into the eventual charge to the passenger.

sections.label: Fare start unclear for PHC drivers
sections.summary: Taxi fares start and stop with the meter, but the point at which the fare starts is unclear for PHC drivers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: For taxis, the fare starts when drivers hit the start button on the meter and stops when drivers stop the meter.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: However, the point at which the fare starts is not clear for PHC drivers.

sections.label: Rules for drivers cancelling passengers
sections.summary: Passengers are charged a penalty fee for cancelling on drivers, but the rules for drivers cancelling on passengers are unclear.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Further, even though passengers are charged a certain penalty fee for cancelling on the drivers, what are the rules for drivers cancelling on passengers?

sections.label: Developing codes of practice process
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry can shed light on the process of developing the codes of practice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry shed light on the process of developing the codes of practice?

sections.label: Mandatory emergency alarm buttons pilot
sections.summary: The passage asks if the Ministry will consider piloting mandatory 24/7 emergency alarm buttons for some street-hail and ride-hail services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Leading ride-hailing platforms, such as Uber, also have them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We can make 24/7 emergency alarm service buttons, which are linked to local authorities, mandatory for all P2P passenger services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry consider piloting this feature for some street-hail and ride-hail services?

sections.label: Harmonising street-hail and ride-hail requirements
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry will consider harmonising this requirement for both street-hail and ride-hail services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry consider harmonising this requirement for both street-hail and ride-hail services?

sections.label: Regulating ride-hail services framework
sections.summary: The Bill proposes a regulatory framework based on passenger access, with two operating licences for street-hail and ride-hail, to ensure consistent application of regulations covering all P2P services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: What are their considerations and guiding principles on how they will regulate ride-hail services?

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, the Bill proposes a new regulatory framework based on how passengers access the vehicles, that is, by hailing on the street or booking via a call centre or online app.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: By issuing two operating licences, one for street-hail and one for ride-hail, the Ministry will be able to ensure more consistent application of regulations covering all P2P services in Singapore.

sections.label: Support for PTC fare regulation
sections.summary: The passage expresses support for the proposal to empower PTC to regulate fares set by ride-hailing operators.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Next, I would like to express my support for the proposal to empower PTC to regulate fares set by ride-hailing operators.

sections.label: Uneven driver age and experience rules
sections.summary: The passage notes that rules on required age and driving experience of drivers are still unevenly applied.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, one area which I noticed the rules are still very unevenly applied is the required age and driving experience of the drivers.

sections.label: Age requirement for PHC drivers
sections.summary: The passage introduces an age requirement of 25 years for PHC drivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: First, to introduce an age requirement of 25 years for PHC drivers.

sections.label: Community transport for those needing help
sections.summary: The passage describes a service for those needing help to move around without a caregiver, provided by nine community providers using specialised vans for about 2,000 monthly trips.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is for those who need help to move around and have no caregiver or whose caregiver is unable to provide support because of their own health and physical conditions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There are currently nine community providers, including Handicapped Welfare Association (HWA), Red Cross and others, which provide the service via specialised vans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They now make about 2,000 such trips monthly.

sections.label: Taxi Subsidy Scheme reimbursement
sections.summary: The scheme reimbursed qualified beneficiaries 35% to 80% of monthly taxi fares, including PHC-registered providers like Grab, with MSF expecting 300 beneficiaries by 2021.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The scheme reimbursed qualified beneficiaries 35% to 80% of their monthly taxi fares, including from PHCs registered with LTA, like Grab.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: MSF expects the number of beneficiaries on TSS to grow to 300 by 2021.

sections.label: MOH care place targets
sections.summary: MOH is on track to meet targets of 6,200 daycare places, 10,000 home care places and 17,000 nursing home beds by 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: MOH is on track to meet targets with 6,200 daycare places, 10,000 home care places and 17,000 nursing home beds by 2020.

sections.label: Broadening transport subsidy schemes
sections.summary: The passage calls for reviewing MET demand, broadening qualifying criteria to include severe mental illness or low cognitive functioning, expanding the Taxi Subsidy Scheme, and training more ride-hail and street-hail drivers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The MET scheme is clearly one that will see an increase in demand with our ageing population and, therefore, needs an urgent review; and (b) to consider broadening the qualifying criteria for these schemes to include those with severe mental illness or low cognitive functioning, given their challenges with taking public transport as well as expand the Taxi Subsidy Scheme to include trips to and from medical appointments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Grab has a Grab Assist option where drivers are trained by AIC to offer additional assistance to seniors and PWDs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I ask that the Government look into broadening these schemes to include more ride-hail and street-hail drivers and providers, so that we can meet the access needs of our society with more frequency and consistency.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A possibility could be requiring ride-hail and street-hail providers to have all or at least a certain substantial percentage of drivers trained in providing for passengers with disabilities through a Code of Practice, under clause 30 of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore has pledged to reduce our greenhouse gas emissions by 16% below business-as-usual (BAU) levels in 2020, and made a further commitment to reduce our emissions intensity by 36% from 2005 levels by 2030, and stabilise our greenhouse gas emissions with the aim of peaking around 2030.

sections.label: Vehicular Emissions Scheme framework
sections.summary: A framework to follow could be the Vehicular Emissions Scheme, which considers a vehicle's emissions of four pollutants and its carbon dioxide emissions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A framework to follow could be the Vehicular Emissions Scheme that takes into consideration a vehicle's emissions of four pollutants and the vehicle's carbon dioxide emissions.

sections.label: Lowering barriers for operators
sections.summary: The passage states that low barriers to entry for new operators, removal of driver exclusivity, and transparent fare communication would allow multi-homing for commuters.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: What are the things that we can do?

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We can make sure that the barriers to entry for new operators are low; in particular, the way in which they engage with the main resource, which is the drivers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The removal of driver exclusivity would be the main lever to ensure the barrier to entry for new operators in the space is low.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Some of the regulations that we are putting in place to make sure that the way in which fares are communicated to commuters is transparent and upfront, will effectively allow multi-homing for commuters, that the commuters themselves are deciding amongst the variety of offers and which to choose.

sections.label: CCCS and MOT oversight
sections.summary: CCCS will have oversight over competition issues and, after the Bill is implemented, will decide how it applies to its previous stance on Uber and Grab.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: To the point about the responsibility between CCCS and MOT, well, very clearly, CCCS will have oversight over the competition issues and will continue to do so.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: And to address a similar point made by Mr Leon Perera, after the Bill is implemented, CCCS will examine the matter, and they will have to come to a decision about how the Bill applies to the previous stance that they had taken with respect to Uber and Grab.

sections.label: Carpool operator licensing rules
sections.summary: Carpool operators are not fully licensed, but those with over 800 vehicles are licensed as a ride-hail sub-class.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We, therefore, have different regulations for carpool operators and we would not be subjecting them to a full licensing regime, provided they continue to operate as carpool operators, as opposed to a full ride-hail operator.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: So, if a carpool operator has more than 800 vehicles on its platform, we will license them as a sub-class of ride-hail service operators and they will be required to ensure that the drivers comply with carpooling regulations so that their carpooling is carried out on a restricted non-commercial basis.

sections.label: Taxi accident rates normalised
sections.summary: Normalised for kilometres travelled and taxis available, taxi accidents stayed at five per 10 million km in 2013 and 2018.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Actually, when we normalise the data, in other words, we take into account the number of kilometres (km) travelled and the number of taxis that are available, there has not been an increase.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: In 2013, for taxis, there were five accidents for every 10 million km travelled.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Five years later, in 2018, this has not changed.

sections.label: PHC inspection regime change
sections.summary: PHC inspections currently match private cars, but in future all PHCs must be inspected annually.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Today, the PHC inspection regime is the same as that for private cars, ranging from once every three years to annually based on the vehicle age.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: However, in future, all PHCs will be required to go for annual inspections.

sections.label: Child seat suggestions for taxis
sections.summary: Mr Louis Ng and Mr Dennis Tan suggested requiring taxis and PHCs to have child seats for children below 1.35 metres.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: On child seats, Mr Louis Ng and Mr Dennis Tan suggested requiring taxis and PHCs to be fitted with child seats when ferrying children below 1.35 metres in height.

sections.label: Extending PTC Act to PHC fares
sections.summary: The PTC Act is being amended to extend its purview over PHC fares, following questions from several Members.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: On fares, there were questions on fare-related regulations by Mr Louis Ng, Mr Gan Thiam Poh, Ms Joan Pereira, Assoc Prof Walter Theseira and Mr Ang Wei Neng.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We are amending the PTC Act to extend its purview over PHC fares.

sections.label: PTC fare regulation intention
sections.summary: The intention is not for PTC to regulate fare levels, set caps or provide algorithms.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The intention is not for PTC to start regulating fare levels nor setting caps nor providing algorithms.

sections.label: Fare evasion and overcharging
sections.summary: The passage states that steps will be taken to deter and prevent fare evasion and overcharging.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: For fare evasion and overcharging, we will step in to deter and prevent fare evasion and overcharging.

sections.label: LTA device regulations and footage
sections.summary: LTA has stringent regulations on device installation and recording access, with a seven-day footage retention limit, independent of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: LTA has stringent regulations in place around the installation of these devices and the access to the recordings and none of this is dependent on the Bill before the House today.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: There is already a seven-day limit on the retention of footage today.

sections.label: PDVLs stopped for Work Pass holders
sections.summary: Since April 2019, PDVLs have not been issued to Work Pass holders.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Since April 2019, we have stopped issuing PDVLs to Work Pass holders.

sections.label: Ages of PHC drivers
sections.summary: Only 4% of PHC drivers are aged 20 to 24, and another 12% are aged 25 to 29.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Only 4% of PHC drivers are between the ages of 20 and 24; another 12% between 25 and 29.

sections.label: No change to COE regimes
sections.summary: The passage states that no change will be made to the COE regimes for taxis and PHCs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: On the COE regimes for taxis and PHCs, we will make no change.

sections.label: Taxi cleaner vehicle commitment
sections.summary: Under LTMP 2040, all taxi companies committed to 100% cleaner vehicles by 2040, an industry-led target under LTMP.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Under LTMP 2040, all taxi companies have committed to 100% cleaner vehicles by 2040, and this is an industry-led target under LTMP.

sections.label: Removing Taxi Availability standards
sections.summary: Taxi Availability standards will be removed and the market will drive availability of services instead.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Mr Ang Hin Kee and Mr Ang Wei Neng, who spoke a little bit about this, will be happy to know that we will be removing the Taxi Availability (TA) standards and we will let the market drive availability of services instead.

sections.label: Street-hail and ride-hail co-existence
sections.summary: Street-hail and ride-hail are allowed to co-exist so commuters can find services matching their needs, with minimum service standards for street-hail.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The approach that we are taking is to allow both street-hail and ride-hail to co-exist, and for subclasses, particularly, for ride-hail services to co-exist, so that the commuter, regardless of whether they are an individual or a family, or a PWD or a person with medical risks, will, in the system and the network, be able to find a service that matches their needs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: On the street-hail side, clearly, it is different because you cannot prebook your ride and you do need a certain minimum level of acceptable service that is a common denominator across the variety of needs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: That is why the regulations specify the minimum boot size for taxis, for example, so that luggage can be carried, or a folded wheelchair can be carried.

sections.label: Aggregated platform information blocking
sections.summary: A platform blocking its information from an aggregated platform would not necessarily compromise regulatory outcomes if drivers and commuters are not affected.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The different services that multi-homing providers and mobility-as-a-service providers are offering, on the face of it, may look similar, but actually have very different underlying business models.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: But if I take the simple example that the Member had suggested, where it is simply about aggregating information and a platform decided to prevent their information from being provided on that aggregated platform, that, in the first instance, would not necessarily compromise our regulatory outcomes that we are trying to achieve, provided it did not then subsequently lead to either the drivers not being able to drive across the platforms, or the commuters not being able to find the information to take rides.

sections.label: Price discrimination in ride-hailing
sections.summary: Price discrimination already happens, and the approach is to let it be if there is adequate choice and good market dynamics.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: On the second point of price discrimination, in truth, it happens already.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The effect, though, what it means is that you will get the same ride as someone next to you who is using the app at the same time, to arrive at a similar destination, for a different price.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: And again, our approach will be that as long as there is adequate choice, relatively good dynamics within the market, we will let it be and see what happens.

sections.label: Grab car seat pricing
sections.summary: A Grab car with a car seat costs $2 more, and $5 more for a child aged one to three.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: For me to go home now is $27; for me to have a Grab car with a car seat is actually only $2 more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: For a Grab car with a car seat for a child aged one to three is extra $5.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: So, it is not three times the price.

sections.label: Taxi restrictions and public consultation
sections.summary: Taxis must carry something at all times, restricting their customer options, and public consultation drew concerns from the commuting public.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The difficulty for taxis though is, truly, that it means they have to carry something with them at all times, and this significantly restricts the options that they have in terms of what they can have as customers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: I would also point out that in our public consultation, a fair amount of the concerns came from the commuting public themselves.

sections.label: Public consultation commuting scenarios
sections.summary: The commuting public raised scenarios in a public consultation, and no compromise could be engineered.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: These are some of the scenarios that were thrown up by the commuting public in our public consultation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: And so, we were unable to engineer a compromise.
